rice.description: Rice is the primary staple food for more than half the world's population. It is a grass species usually grown in flooded fields.

ideal_conditions.climate: Hot and humid climate with prolonged sunshine and an assured supply of water.
ideal_conditions.soil: Clayey or clay-loams with good water retention.

planting_tips: Pre-germinate seeds before sowing in the nursery.
Transplant seedlings after 21-25 days.
Maintain standing water of 2-5 cm in the field during the early growth stage.
care_maintenance: Apply Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium (NPK) in split doses.
Control weeds manually or using herbicides within the first 45 days.
Monitor for pests like Stem Borer and Brown Plant Hopper.
rice.harvesting: Harvest when the grain turns golden yellow and moisture content is around 20%.

maize.description: Maize, or corn, is a cereal grain known as the 'Queen of Cereals' due to its high genetic yield potential.

ideal_conditions.soil: Well-drained loamy or sandy loam soil rich in organic matter.

planting_tips: Plant seeds 2-5 cm deep in rows.
Ensure proper spacing (60x20 cm) for adequate sunlight and air.
Best sown at the onset of monsoon or spring.
care_maintenance: Maize is a heavy feeder; ensure adequate nitrogen supply.
Keep the field weed-free for the first 40 days.
Ensure moisture during flowering and grain filling stages.
maize.harvesting: Harvest when husks turn dry and brown, and kernels are hard.

wheat.description: Wheat is a widespread cereal grain and a major source of vegetable protein worldwide.

ideal_conditions.climate: Cool and moist weather during growth, warm and dry during ripening.
ideal_conditions.soil: Well-drained clay loam or loamy texture.

planting_tips: Sow seeds 4-5 cm deep.
Treat seeds with fungicides before sowing to prevent soil-borne diseases.
Timely sowing is critical for optimal yield.
care_maintenance: Apply irrigation at critical stages: Crown Root Initiation (CRI) and Flowering.
Use split application of urea.
Watch for termite attacks in dry areas.
wheat.harvesting: Harvest when the grain hardens and straw turns golden and brittle.

cotton.description: Cotton is a soft, fluffy staple fiber and the most widely used natural fiber cloth in the world.

ideal_conditions.climate: Tropical and subtropical patterns; requires long frost-free periods.
ideal_conditions.soil: Black cotton soil (regur) or well-drained alluvial soil.

planting_tips: Sow seeds when soil temperature is above 15°C.
Maintain proper spacing to avoid overcrowding and humidity buildup.
Use pest-resistant varieties (like Bt Cotton) if available.
care_maintenance: Thinning should be done to keep healthy plants.
Requires regular weeding and hoeing.
Manage pests like Bollworms and Aphids aggressively.
cotton.harvesting: Pick cotton bolls when fully open and dry, preferably in the morning.

sugarcane.description: Sugarcane is a tall perennial grass used for sugar production.

ideal_conditions.soil: Deep, well-drained loams or heavy clays.

planting_tips: Plant using stem cuttings (setts) with at least 3 buds.
Treat setts with fungicide before planting.
Deep furrow planting is recommended.
care_maintenance: Heavy feeder; requires high Nitrogen and Potassium.
Earthing up is done to support the plant and prevent lodging.
Frequent irrigation is needed during the growing phase.
sugarcane.harvesting: Harvest when cane matures (lower leaves dry up and juice Brix is high).

pulses.description: Pulses (Lentils, Chickpeas, Beans) are distinct from vegetable crops and harvestable solely for the dry grain.

ideal_conditions.climate: Cool and dry climate for most varieties.
ideal_conditions.soil: Light loamy or sandy soils with good drainage.

planting_tips: Rhizobium culture seed treatment increases nitrogen fixation.
Avoid waterlogging as pulses are sensitive to excess moisture.
care_maintenance: Requires less nitrogen fixation but needs Phosphorus.
One or two irrigations during branching and pod development.
Protect from pod borers.
pulses.harvesting: Harvest when pods turn brown and hard.

millet.description: Millets are coarse grains, highly nutritious and known as 'Nutri-Cereals'.

ideal_conditions.climate: Warm and dry climate; highly drought-resistant.
ideal_conditions.soil: Sandy loam or shallow black soils; can grow in poor soils.

planting_tips: Prepare fine seedbed.
Sow shallow (2-3 cm).
care_maintenance: Minimal fertilizer required compared to other cereals.
Thinning is necessary to maintain population.
Avoid water stagnation.

potato.description: Potato is a root vegetable and the fourth largest food crop.

ideal_conditions.soil: Loose, well-drained, sandy loam rich in organic matter.

planting_tips: Use disease-free seed tubers.
Plant in ridges to allow tuber expansion.
care_maintenance: Earthing up is essential to cover tubers and prevent greening.
Protect from Late Blight disease.
Stop irrigation 10 days before harvest.
potato.harvesting: Harvest when vines die back and skin of tuber hardens.

tomato.description: Tomato is an edible berry of the plant Solanum lycopersicum.

ideal_conditions.climate: Warm season crop; cannot withstand frost.

planting_tips: Transplant seedlings when they have 4-5 true leaves.
Stake tall varieties (indeterminate) for support.
care_maintenance: Mulching helps retain moisture and control weeds.
Consistent watering prevents Blossom End Rot.
Prune suckers to encourage fruit growth.
tomato.harvesting: Harvest at breaker or red ripe stage depending on market distance.

barley.description: Barley is a major cereal grain grown in temperate climates globally.

ideal_conditions.soil: Sandy loam to saline-sodic soils (salt tolerant).

planting_tips: Often grown as a rabi (winter) crop in India.
Prepare land to fine tilth.
care_maintenance: Needs nitrogen for vegetative growth.
Sensitive to waterlogging.
Requires 2-3 irrigations.
